topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that all living things are composed of one or more cells that support life processes, as described by the cell theory. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that all living things are composed of one or more cells that support life processes, as described by the cell theory. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: the development of the cell theory demonstrates the nature of science;
cell structure and organelles support life processes;
similarities and differences between plant and animal cells determine how they support life processes;
cell division is the mechanism for growth and reproduction; and
cellular transport (osmosis and diffusion) is important for life processes.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that there are levels of structural organization in living things. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that there are levels of structural organization in living things. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: patterns of cellular organization support life processes;
unicellular and multicellular organisms have comparative structures; and
similar characteristics determine the classification of organisms.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that there are chemical processes of energy transfer which are important for life. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that there are chemical processes of energy transfer which are important for life. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: photosynthesis is the foundation of virtually all food webs; and
photosynthesis and cellular respiration support life processes.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that biotic and abiotic factors affect an ecosystem. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that biotic and abiotic factors affect an ecosystem. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: matter moves through ecosystems via the carbon, water, and nitrogen cycles;
energy flow is represented by food webs and energy pyramids; and
relationships exist among producers, consumers, and decomposers.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that populations in a biological community interact and are interdependent. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that populations in a biological community interact and are interdependent. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: relationships exist between predators and prey and these relationships are modeled in food webs;
the availability and use of resources may lead to competition and cooperation;
symbiotic relationships support the survival of different species; and
the niche of each organism supports survival.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that adaptations support an organism's survival in an ecosystem. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that adaptations support an organism's survival in an ecosystem. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: biotic and abiotic factors define land, marine, and freshwater ecosystems; and
physical and behavioral characteristics enable organisms to survive within a specific ecosystem.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that ecosystems, communities, populations, and organisms are dynamic and change over time. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that ecosystems, communities, populations, and organisms are dynamic and change over time. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: organisms respond to daily, seasonal, and long-term changes;
changes in the environment may increase or decrease population size; and
large-scale changes such as eutrophication, climate changes, and catastrophic disturbances affect ecosystems.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that relationships exist between ecosystem dynamics and human activity. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that relationships exist between ecosystem dynamics and human activity. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: changes in habitat can disturb populations;
disruptions in ecosystems can change species competition; and
variations in biotic and abiotic factors can change ecosystems.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that organisms reproduce and transmit genetic information to new generations. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that organisms reproduce and transmit genetic information to new generations. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: DNA has a role in making proteins that determine organism traits;
the role of meiosis is to transfer traits to the next generation; and
Punnett squares are mathematical models used to predict the probability of traits in offspring.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that populations of organisms can change over time. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that populations of organisms can change over time. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: mutation, adaptation, natural selection, and extinction change populations;
the fossil record, genetic information, and anatomical comparisons provide evidence for evolution; and
environmental factors and genetic variation, influence survivability and diversity of organisms.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that matter is composed of atoms. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that matter is composed of atoms. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: our understanding of atoms has developed over time;
the periodic table can be used to predict the chemical and physical properties of matter; and
the kinetic molecular theory is used to predict and explain matter interactions.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that matter has properties and is conserved in chemical and physical processes. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that matter has properties and is conserved in chemical and physical processes. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: pure substances can be identified based on their chemical and physical properties;
pure substances can undergo physical and chemical changes that may result in a change of properties;
compounds form through ionic and covalent bonding; and
balanced chemical equations model the conservation of matter.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that the periodic table is a model used to organize elements based on their atomic structure. Key uses include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that the periodic table is a model used to organize elements based on their atomic structure. Key uses include

outcomes.text: symbols, atomic numbers, atomic mass, chemical groups (families), and periods are identified on the periodic table; and
elements are classified as metals, metalloids, and nonmetals.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that energy is conserved. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that energy is conserved. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: energy can be stored in different ways;
energy is transferred and transformed; and
energy can be transformed to meet societal needs.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that waves are important in the movement of energy. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that waves are important in the movement of energy. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: energy may be transferred in the form of longitudinal and transverse waves;
mechanical waves need a medium to transfer energy;
waves can interact; and
energy associated with waves has many applications.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that electromagnetic radiation has characteristics. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that electromagnetic radiation has characteristics. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: electromagnetic radiation, including visible light, has wave characteristics and behavior; and
regions of the electromagnetic spectrum have specific characteristics and uses.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that work, force, and motion are related. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that work, force, and motion are related. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: motion can be described using position and time; and
motion is described by Newton's laws.

topics.title: The student will investigate and understand that there are basic principles of electricity and magnetism. Key ideas include

subtopics.title: The student will investigate and understand that there are basic principles of electricity and magnetism. Key ideas include

outcomes.text: an imbalance of charge generates static electricity;
materials have different conductive properties;
electric circuits transfer energy;
magnetic fields model the magnetic effects of certain materials;
electric current and magnetic fields are related; and
many technologies use electricity and magnetism.
